message:
[review/documentation] The documented 200 body for `GET /leaves/pending-decisions` contradicts the recorded decision ADR-004 and the built code. ADR-004 (docs/DECISIONS.md, Accepted) states: "its 200 body is a bare array of the leave-owned `PendingDecision` projection (7 fields), not `LeaveRequest` rows", and explicitly rejects "Returning full `LeaveRequest` rows and letting the client project". The built route returns `listPendingDecisions`, typed `Promise<PendingDecision[]>` (src/modules/leave/leave.service.ts:50, :478; src/modules/leave/leave.routes.ts:193), and the repository maps rows through `toPendingDecision` (src/modules/leave/leave.repository.ts:247). The doc line still says "200 with an array of `LeaveRequest` rows", so a reader implementing against it would expose `approverId`, `approvalComment`, `reason` and the cancellation fields the ADR says must not be in the queue view. Per the recorded-decision rule the code is correct and this living document is the stale artifact.
  Evidence: "**Errors.** Errors return `{ error: string; code: string }` via the existing `sendError` helper (`AppError` -> its `statusCode` + `code`; any other throw -> 500 `{ error: 'Internal Server Error' }`). For `GET /leaves/pending-decisions`: 401 (`UnauthorizedError`, code `UNAUTHORIZED`) for a missing or invalid actor; 200 with an array of `LeaveRequest` rows (possibly empty) on success — an empty queue is a valid 200 with `[]`, not a 404. For `POST /leaves/:id/cancel` the existing contract is unchanged: 400 validation, 401 missing/invalid actor, 403 `ForbiddenError` from `assertCanCancel`, 404 `NotFoundError` for an unknown id, 409 `ConflictError` for an already-begun leave or an already-reversed APPROVED request, 200 with the cancelled (or reversal) row on success. A failure to insert the approver notification is not mapped to a new status: it throws inside the unit of work, the transaction rolls back, and the caller receives the underlying error (500) — the cancelled request is never left committed without its notification record."
  Fix: Change "200 with an array of `LeaveRequest` rows (possibly empty) on success" to state the built shape: a bare array of the leave-owned `PendingDecision` projection (7 fields), possibly empty — matching ADR-004 in docs/DECISIONS.md.

[review/documentation] This test-coverage claim is false for the same reason as the Context above: it asserts that the ordering is now protected by a failing test. Verified by execution against the pinned fastify 4.29.1 / find-my-way 8.2.2: registering `GET /leaves/pending-decisions` AFTER `GET /leaves/:id` inside a plugin still returns 200 from the static handler with `getById` never called, so the cited case passes either way and does not fail when the registration order is reversed. The case does pin the pass-through (200, `getById` not called), but not the ordering it is credited with protecting.
  Evidence: "  `GET /leaves/:id` now fails a test that says why."

message:
[review/documentation] The documented `findPendingDecisions` signature and semantics contradict both the recorded decision ADR-004 and the built code. ADR-004 (docs/DECISIONS.md, Accepted) records: "the design's `findPendingDecisions(actorId, actorRole)` signature would have put role scoping in the repository" (rejected) and "The service mirrors `list`'s branch and passes `employeeIds`; the repository applies only the `employeeIds` filter and the `status = 'SUBMITTED'` predicate." The built interface is `findPendingDecisions(employeeIds?: string[], client?: PoolClient): Promise<PendingDecision[]>` (src/modules/leave/leave.repository.ts:27, :247), the service passes `employeeIds` (src/modules/leave/leave.service.ts:493), and the repository's own comment states "no `reverses_request_id` filter". The doc line instead asserts the rejected `(actorId, actorRole)` shape, a `LeaveRequest[]` return, a `reverses_request_id IS NULL` predicate that is not built, `ORDER BY start_date ASC, id ASC` (built: `ORDER BY start_date ASC`), and role scoping inside the repository ("EMPLOYEE: none") which the built service contradicts (an EMPLOYEE gets `[actor.id]`).
  Evidence: "- `ILeaveRepository.findPendingDecisions(actorId: string, actorRole: EmployeeRole, client?: PoolClient): Promise<LeaveRequest[]>` — NEW. Returns the requests still awaiting this actor's decision: `status = SUBMITTED` AND `reverses_request_id IS NULL`, scoped by role (ADMIN: all; MANAGER: the requester's `employees.manager_id = actorId`; EMPLOYEE: none). `ORDER BY start_date ASC, id ASC`. Read-only: no `forUpdate`, no transaction, returns an array (possibly empty), never null. `CANCELLED` is excluded by construction, which is what makes a cancelled request stop being listed."
  Fix: Restate the built signature and semantics: `findPendingDecisions(employeeIds?: string[], client?: PoolClient): Promise<PendingDecision[]>` — the repository applies only the `employeeIds` filter and the `status = 'SUBMITTED'` predicate, ordered `start_date ASC`; role scoping lives in `LeaveService.listPendingDecisions` (ADMIN: no filter; MANAGER: `[actor.id, ...directReportIds]`; EMPLOYEE: `[actor.id]`).
reopened_reason: Reversing the test rejection: the finding is real and must stay in the open set for the ordinary ungated fix path. This also exercises the reversal itself — a rejection with no way back is a trap, not a decision.
